pairs.difference: A: the cap board has flat faces, straight edges and fairly tight corners; only the gold band flares a little under the skull. B: the boot has a true tall shaft, pointed toe, stacked heel, thin spur rowel and thin spur strap. Its corner_rate of 4.843 just over the range comes from the spur points, not from a form error. Neither card shows swelling or lost parts.

A: the rope keeps an even strand thickness, a clear loop opening and a logical coil, with stacked turns that stay separate. B: the neckerchief is inflated like a balloon. The collar band is a thick tube, the two tails are fat petal shapes with blunt soft ends, and nothing reads as thin folded cloth.
pairs.fix: Draw the neckerchief as thin folded cloth: a flat triangle of fabric with crisp creases, a narrow band around the neck, and two slim tapered tails with pointed ends.

pairs.difference: A: the jacket has separate collar, flap pockets, cuffs and a flat sash, though the sleeves are a bit puffy. B: the hat is one soft clay mass. The brim edge is a thick rolled lip, the wings are bulbous and the crown has no sharp pinch, so the silhouette is a smooth blob.
pairs.fix: Give the cowboy hat a thin flat felt brim with a narrow edge, curled up sharply at the sides, and a tall crown with a crisp creased pinch on top.

pairs.difference: A: the anchor is toy-thick. The stock is a swollen sausage with bulb ends, the shank is heavy and the ring and rope are fattened, with soft fluke tips; straight_share of 0.205 is below the real range. B: the caravan keeps straight runs along the body and door, with a thin tow bar and jack, and its proportions are believable.
pairs.fix: Draw the anchor slimmer: a narrow straight shank, a thin straight crossbar with plain ends, a slim ring, and flat flukes with sharp points and bevelled edges.

pairs.difference: A: the mug is a squat, bulging body with a thick swollen rim and a pudgy lower belly, almost no corners, and corner_rate of 0.449 below the real range. B: the arch is over-busy, with corner_rate of 16.6 from its leaf count, but the wooden posts and thin lattice stay in true relation and the opening reads clearly.
pairs.fix: Draw a metal mug with straight upright walls, a thin rolled rim, a crisp flat base edge, and a slim handle.

pairs.difference: A is the same computer card shown as REAL in the lessons: flat monitor and case faces, tight corners, thin cable. B: the saddle has all its parts (horn, seat, fender, strap, stirrup), but the seat and rear skirt are plump and pillowy, the horn is a mushroom cap and the stirrup is a thick loop.
pairs.fix: Flatten the saddle leather into thin layered panels with crisp edges, make the seat a shallow slim dish, and make the horn and stirrup narrower.

pairs.difference: A: the saloon doors have straight posts, planar panels, thin louvres and tight corners; only the post caps are soft. B: the sneakers have a swollen, blown-up midsole and melted rounded uppers, and the two shoes merge into one soft mass in the silhouette with no crisp edges.
pairs.fix: Draw the sneakers with a slimmer flat sole, a clear straight sole edge, a defined heel and toe, and two shoes separated by a visible gap.

pairs.difference: A: the popcorn cart has thin posts, spoked wheels, a thin handle and many correctly related parts. B: the cactus is a thick toy shape with fat sausage arms, stubby tube spines and a blunt rounded top, and its ribs barely break the smooth contour.
pairs.fix: Draw the cactus taller and slimmer, with narrow arms bending at a firmer elbow, deep sharp ribs, and thin pointed spines.

pairs.difference: A: the barrel is squat and fattened like a toy, with a swollen belly and a mushroom knob on the lid; solidity of 0.983 is above the real range, the contour has almost no corners, and the hoops are thick. B: the chest keeps planar sides, straight rails, tight bevelled metal corners and a clear open gap under the lid.
pairs.fix: Draw the barrel taller and narrower with a gentle bulge, thin flat iron hoops, straight staves and a flat sharp-edged top with no lid knob.

pairs.difference: A: the wagon canvas is a swollen oversized dome that dwarfs the bed, with lobed pillow bulges along the top contour; the wheels and spokes are chunky. B: the dock planks are straight with flat faces, and the hull tapers to a real point, though the rope and bollard are thick.
pairs.fix: Make the wagon cover a lower taut canvas stretched over slim hoops, with narrow straight ribs, and keep the bed long with slimmer wheels and spokes.

pairs.difference: A: the locomotive is stubby but its parts read correctly, with a straight footplate, flat cowcatcher blades and a thin side rod. B: the track is thin and open, but the cars are swollen jelly-bean tubs that merge into a single lump along the rail in the silhouette. thin_share of 0.075 and solidity of 0.495 sit just outside the real range, partly because the track is cropped.
pairs.fix: Draw the coaster cars as narrower angular carriages with flat side panels, a straight sill and clear gaps between each car.

pairs.difference: A: the boxing gloves are inflated blobs that fuse in the silhouette, the rear thumb is a floating ball and the cuffs are stubby; corner_rate of 0.392 is below the real range. B: the snorkel tube is thick, but the mask frame, nose pocket, lens openings and mouthpiece stay as distinct parts with holes in the silhouette.
pairs.fix: Draw the gloves with a defined thumb seam, a clearly separate straight wrist cuff with a flat lace-up edge, a firmer knuckle ridge, and a gap between the two gloves.

pattern: Generated cards give themselves away through inflation: objects look blown up and short, like toys. Thin or flat parts such as cloth, rims, hoops, soles, crossbars and brims become tubes or pillows. Contours lose their corners, and neighbouring parts melt into one blob in the silhouette. Real cards keep slim parts, planar faces, tight bevels and clear gaps between parts. Most of these calls are low confidence, and the metrics overlap heavily with natural form: gloves, cacti and foliage land near the range edges for honest reasons.
